Comments: On 06/16/2025, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the HIXENBAUGH 1-P060 OG well in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County. The toe of the slope failure is within access road drainage channel (Photo 1-5). On 04/17/2024 (SAIR 3741762) and 05/10/2024 (SAIR 3760574) stabilization and remediation to access road and channel slope was conducted.-I observed erosion rills and ruts along the access road. I recommend maintenance to access road (Photo 6 and 7).-A well tag was observed on the well head. Some corrosion was observed on well head (Photo 8 and 9).-The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h) (Photo 10).-Some corrosion was observed on the production equipment. It appears production equipment was leaking. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed (Photo 11 and 12).-I observed Low Ash Gas Engine Oil/fuel appears to be leaking onto the ground below next to compressor station. I recommend remediation and maintenance to well site (Photo 13-17,20).-Some corrosion was observed on the production tank (Photo 18 and 19).Determination:Violations are being issued for slope failure along access road: 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, and 78.53. Violations are being issued for fuel leaking onto well site. The operator failed to report: 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.54, and SWMA 301

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-18 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-18
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 877468
Permit API: 117-21999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: An inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a spill of produced water to the pad surface from a cam lock fitting between a produced water tank and a battery of frac tanks. The operator estimated the volume of the spill at 15 gallons. I met with Jen Compton of Rockdale upon arriving on location. She showed me the area where the spill occurred and impacted the pad surface. She stated that the cam lock fitting on the northern-most produced water tank was found leaking on the morning of 2/17/20. She said that the produced water flowed south toward the other produced water tank. She said that some excavation was already performed but the area in front of the south produced water tank is continuously collecting fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC). She said that it appeared that fluid is flowing out from underneath the south produced water tank and flowing into the area in front of the tank. A vaccuum truck was present on location during this inspection and was sucking up the fluid as it seeped into the area in front of the south tank. Ms. Compton also said that there was a truck driver on location one hour before the leak was discovered which leads them to believe that the fitting leaked for 1 hour at most. I took several EC readings in front of the south produced water tank where fluid was pooling. Every EC reading was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. No other substantial volume of water was present in the area near the produced water tanks. When I looked beneath the south tank, the gravel appeared to be saturated with fluid. It appeared that the fluid pooling in front of the tank was coming from beneath the south produced water tank. The areas Ms. Compton said had already been excavated were covered with approximately one half inch of snow. These areas appeared dry other than the snow. I took a sample, #0718-160, from the area in front of the south produced water tank which were sent to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department requests a justification for the reported spill volume. The Department recommends moving the south produced water tank to assess the soil beneath it and vacuum the fluid there as needed. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the surface area of the pad which appears to have been impacted. Violations noted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/12/2022 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Twp, Tioga county. 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus.  In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/12/2022
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 951612
Permit API: 117-22128
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/12/2022
Comments: Warm/sunny at time of inspection with light wind. At time of inspection crews were on location moving production equipment to make room for pad expansion. During the inspection Mike Panettieri (OGI supervisor) and myself (OGI) spoke to Ross Schmidt (District Superintendent) for Seneca Resources. At time of inspection annulus vents were checked for presence/absence of gas. The results for each annulus vent are as follows. 9x5 = 100% LEL and 20% Methane/vol 13x9 = 35% LEL and 10% Methane/vol 20x13 = 100% LEL and 5% Methane/vol (about 24 bubbles per minute) The Department’s investigation of the Cruttenden 33HU well found that combustible gas is currently venting outside the surface casing string. This is a violation of the Department’s regulations relating to Cement Standards, 25 Pa. Code ¿78a.85(a)(5), which provides: "When cementing surface casing or coal protective casing, the operator shall use cement that meets or exceeds the ASTM International C 150, Type I, II, or III Standard or API Specification 10. The cement must also: (5) Prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used." Please note that because Seneca provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code ¿78a.86 (defective cement), for the annuli where combustible gas was observed during this inspection. However, Seneca is required to comply with the Department’s regulations, 25 Pa. Code ¿78a.86, which provides: "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿ 78.91 – 78.98 (related to plugging)." Therefore, please provide a written description detailing how Seneca intends to comply with this regulation within 30 days of receipt of this inspection report. Also, please include information regarding the suspected source of the stray gas."

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/09/2024 to GREYLOCK PROD LLC in Hector Township, Potter county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/09/2024
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8210423
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2024
Comments: On 12/09/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1200 hours, weather was 40F and raining. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Stimulation activities for the two recently drilled wells are ongoing, equipment is located onsite to support these activities (photos #2-5). See inspection report #3878285 for more details. The accessible area excavated due to the release noted in inspection report #3878285 has been backfilled and fluids in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~701-741us/cm (photo #6). The remaining impacted area from this release will be excavated and backfilled upon removal of the rig matting covering that area. DEP Environmental Cleanups and Brownsfield personnel were onsite prior to my arrival to follow up on the release detailed in inspection report #3878285 and noted concerns regarding a diesel sheen observed on portions of the pad surface.The source of the diesel was investigated by Greylock and it was determined that a maintenance truck located onsite had released an undetermined amount of diesel, the truck was removed from the site and staff were working on removing diesel from the pad surface at the time of this inspection (photos #7-10). Fluid was observed overtopping from the secondary containment structure of the produced fluids offload area onsite (photos #11 and 12). This fluid was combining with rainwater and the diesel sheen on the pad surface and moving into the pad's drainage system which transports water from the pad surface to the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control. Fluids on the pad surface near the offload containment structure field measured for EC at ~10.32-15.93mS/cm; personnel from Penn E and R measured a similar result of 11.10mS/cm (photos #14-16).The pad drainage system services the site's infiltration basin via two pipes which move fluids from their respective half of the pad (photo #17). One pipe is located closer to the produced fluids offload area and the other is located near the wellheads. Fluid with a diesel sheen was observed discharging into the infiltration basin from the pipe near the offload area; this fluid field measured for EC at ~1.35mS/cm and the soil near this area field measured for EC at ~1.20mS/cm (photos #18-20). Fluid discharging from the pipe near the wellheads field measured for EC at ~0.908mS/cm (photo #21). Vacuum trucks were dispatched to remove fluids from the secondary containment structures and the pad surface in response to the release (photo #22). Personnel were also working to install sump pumps and shut in the drainage pipes to prevent any further discharge into the basin.I followed up with Greylock and they informed me that the drains discharging into the basin were shut in at 1400 hours and they were recovering fluids from basin with a vacuum truck.The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to prevent fluids from reaching PCSM controls until all contaminated fluids and soils are recovered.-Removing fluids from containment structures as it accumulates.-Following Act 2 to remediate the infiltration basin, diesel spill, and produced fluids containment release.Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #105-21962:-25 PA 78a64a(f) due to the observation of produced fluids overtopping from a secondary containment structure and being conveyed into the sites PCSM controls. -35 P.S. 691.401 due to the release of produced fluids and diesel discharging into the site's PCSM controls.The violations cited in inspection report #3878285 remain outstanding due to the remediation requirements outlined in 25 PA 78a.66(c)(2)(i) having not yet been met.I departed the site at 1345.

SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus. This is indicative of defective cement. Since the presence of gas was detected in the HUNTER 5H well (20x13) annulus was not addressed in previous responses received, the Dept. requests in writing, by 7/4/20, how CALLC plans to address this defective condition.

Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.

Violation ID: 8261806
Permit API: 059-26510
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: On 01/13/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 01/02/2026 at the NV48 Well Site. The Department first received notification of the spill 01/09/2026 from CNX (CTS 39456). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb (PA DEP), Melissa Cherry of Penn E and R, SPSI, and CNX representative Joe Fletcher.Per CNX, spill was said to have been reported to the Departments emergency hotline on 01/02/2026 via the 1 (800) 541-2050 phone number, however the Department did not have a history of a notification. Justin Ruth of CNX submitted a call log of the call, which occurred at 5:48 PM on 01/02/2026.On 01/09/2026, Chad Eisenman of CNX notified the Department of the spill; it was reported that 5 bbls of combined brine and freshwater released onto the pad at the NV48 Well Site on 01/02/2026. The spill was identified at approximately 3:48 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 5:58 PM. Soil and gravel were impacted on the pad, the spill was contained to the pad, and no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. CNX is utilizing the alternative spill remediation standards under Act 2.The following was observed during inspection:The spill originated from two produced water tanks (brine) on containment, and a freshwater tank. Produced fluid back-fed into the freshwater tank, and the combined fluids released out of the freshwater tank onto the pad. 5 barrels (bbls) were released (Photo 1).The majority of the impacted material on the pad has been remediated. The impacted area furthest from the tanks yielded conductivity readings ranging from 98.6 - 551 S/cm (Photos 2-6).The surface material was scraped and removed, and trenches/sumps were dug. Conductivity readings within the trenches yielded readings ranging from 1148 S/cm - 3.46 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).Conductivity readings closer to the tanks and the front section of the impacted area ranged from 1469 S/cm - 7.41 mS/cm (Photos 12-18).The area was still in the process of remediation; however it was anticipated to be done the day of the Departments inspection (Photos 19-21).A background conductivity reading was obtained near the edge of the pad. The reading was 655 S/cm (Photos 22, 23).It was noted on site that the roll off dumpster was the fifth one to be used for the waste. I observed incorrect labeling on the roll off (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan were both at the site entrance (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid combined with freshwater over a barrel, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: On April 19, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an investigation of a reported spill (CTS No. 356072) at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported on April 19, 2021, after removing the second AST off the well pad an area of high conductivity and staining was observed in the highly compacted soil where the tank was located. The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. A contractor was onsite beginning to excavate the impacted soils. The contractor was removing about 6 to 8 inches of impacted soil. The area of impact was screened by Beech Resources for conductivity. Areas where the compacted soil had already been removed had a conductivity near 320 uS/cm to 910 uS/cm. Conductivity of areas that had not yet been excavated at the time were around 1.69 mS/cm. There were no seeps off the well pad observed. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection Reports 3139277 and 3141035 still remain.

Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township

Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: The purpose of this routine inspection is to document a surface water encroachment resulting from the construction of the Akins Lease Akins #3 OG Well well pad. The well permit for Akins #3 was not observed anywhere onsite at the time of this inspection. Surface permitting biologists Samantha Lutz (DEP) and Jessica McDuff (DEP) were onsite for the duration of the inspection to confirm findings documented in the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection (Inspection # 4028638). Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) was also present. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) arrived midway through the inspection.TMP opted to ignore advice given through the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection report and an 08/26/2025 field meeting. During the 08/26/2025 field meeting I advised Kyle Miller of the existing surface concerns in the vicinity of the staked well location, and made recommendations for maintaining appropriate setback distances per chapter 105 regulations.At the time of this inspection, it was observed that the well pad was constructed atop an unnamed tributary of Jackson Run pictured in the 08/04/2025 inspection images. The defined bed and banks of this stream are visible above the cut bank of the constructed well pad (Image 4), which suggests that excavation of the stream bed occurred during the construction of this well pad. It was also observed that dirt and gravel fill material was used to build up the site of the well pad atop the stream.A diversion ditch was constructed along the upslope perimeter of the well pad for the conveyance of roadway and well pad runoff, and apparently to accept the flow of the tributary stream that terminates abruptly on the cut bank of the well pad. This diversion ditch is then directed into a culvert on the west edge of the well site (Image 2). The outflow of the culvert appears to return to the defined bed and banks of the unnamed tributary of Jackson Run. Several erosion and sediment control concerns are present in this current configuration.A pit has been excavated on the well pad. Title 25, Chapters 78.61 and 78.62 outline the requirements for the use of a pit as a disposal area for drill cuttings and residual waste generated during the development of a conventional well. These regulations state that a disposal area may not be located within 100 feet of either a stream or wetland. The use of this pit as a disposal area would be in violation of the aforementioned regulations.A notice of violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection for the failure to obtain the appropriate Chapter 105 permit(s) prior to the construction of a water encroachment and for the failure to post the well permit during the construction of the well pad and its access road. In order to achieve compliance with respect to the Chapter 105.11 violation, an application for the appropriate Chapter 105 permit will need to be submitted and ultimately issued. It is requested that TMP produce for the Department surveyed site maps depicting the as-built configuration of all recent construction activities that have occurred on the Akins lease including road improvement/widening of existing lease roads, access road construction, and well pad construction for both the proposed Akins #3 OG well and the un-permitted Akins #4 proposed well.It is requested that TMP produce for the Department a full stream and wetland delineation in the vicinity of construction activities on the Akins lease. It is expected that the findings of such a delineation be documented on site maps depicting each stream, wetland, and drainage feature.It is requested that TMP report the acreage of earth disturbance resulting from the recent construction activities on the Akins lease, including road improvement/widening of existing lease roads.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/09/2025
Violation Code: 102.5(m)4 - PERMIT REQUIREMENTS – GENERAL PERMITS – Person failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the E & S Control General Permit.
Violation ID: 8228896
Permit API: 125-29133
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Blaine Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/09/2025
Comments: On April 9, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. An Erosion and Sediment (E and S) individual permit was issued by the Department for the site on January 26, 2024 and expires on January 25, 2029. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad and upslope of the northern corner of the well pad, which was reported to the Department by the operator on April 7, 2025. Range Resources representative Dennis Furmanek was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Stimulation operations are ongoing at the well pad at the time of this inspection (see photos 3 and 18). All containers onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within well pad secondary containment (see photo 20). All secondary containment onsite appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection with no holes or tears observed. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 23). The GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 24). Some areas of minor staining were observed on the surface of the well pad during this inspection. The E and S inspection log, E and S plan drawings, Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan, E and S individual permit approval letter, secondary containment inspection, log, and well permits are onsite (see photos 19 and 25). Upon review onsite, the ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the information required by 78a.55.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 2). The soil crack that was reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present on the southwestern fill slope of well pad (see photos 4-9). It appears to be approximately 15 feet in length with saturated ground down slope of it, and no toe bulge observed below at the time of inspection. The Schwotzer to Hoskins pipeline is being constructed west of the well pad (see photo 11). The slough that was also reported by the operator on 4/07/2025 was present up slope of the northern corner of well pad (see photos 12-16). The operator estimates this area of soil movement to be approximately 25 feet wide by 30 feet long. This slough appears to pose the potential to threaten a stormwater channel down slope of it, if the displaced soil continues to move (see photo 17). Mr. Furmanek reported during this inspection that the operator intends to conduct repairs on these areas of soil movement once stimulation operations have been completed onsite and weather conditions allow for it. CFS that appears to be in need of maintenance was observed along the northeastern edge of the well pad (see photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends the operator conduct general maintenance and housekeeping onsite to address the minor staining onsite and CFS maintenance needed. The Department also recommends that the operator monitor the soil crack on the southwestern fill slope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on the soil exposed by the slough north of the well pad.Violations shall be issued against the slough north of the well pad which could pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. See NOV Response Comments.

Violation ID: 8164960
Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/08/2023
Comments: On 11/08/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well. The following was observed:Operator and well information on site (Photos 1, 2). I recommend placing the rest of the well information on the same sign that has the operator information.Pumpjack in motion upon arrival, some grease/oil on gravel. I recommend removal (Photo 3). Wellhead, production equipment were in generally good condition (Photos 2-5). Mild corrosion. Additional equipment adjacent to the well approximately 40 feet away - there is a depression around the equipment and it is filled with water; dead vegetation around depression, no high conductivity reading. I recommend addressing the depression and exploring the cause of the depression and dead vegetation - unclear if cause if from equipment or pooled water (Photos 6).Downslope of the well were five production tanks within an earthen berm. The berm was in generally good condition, however the pooled water within the berm contained high conductivity readings, specifically in front of tank 1. The sediment within the berm had adequate readings, however the rest of the pooled water had slightly elevated readings. A slightly elevated conductivity reading was taken within the gravel/sediment below the valve of tank 5. This area was relatively small and is recommended that any affected material is removed and disposed of properly. A corroded piece of equipment noted near tank 5 (Photos 7-22, see captions for specific locations). I notified the operator while onsite; a vac truck later was there removing the fluid as I was leaving. Plans are to add equipment to catch fluids when the vac truck removes the hose from the valves. It is noted that the access road has multiple uses, including agricultural, however the access roads to the well sites require routine monitoring and maintenance.Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the pooled water and prompt remediation, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and were immediately corrected. A follow up inspection to ensure there is not residual production fluids within the berm. No additional violations are being issued right now, however additional violations may be forthcoming.
